entities.summary: David Murphy-Kasim Greenwood was an American professional basketball player whose National Basketball Association (NBA) career spanned 12 years from 1979 to 1991. He played college basketball for the UCLA Bruins, earning consensus All-American honors twice in 1978 and 1979. Greenwood was selected by the Chicago Bulls in the first round of the 1979 NBA draft with the second overall pick. He was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team with the Bulls during the 1979–80 season. A forward/center, he also played in the NBA with the San Antonio Spurs, Denver Nuggets and Detroit Pistons.
